history.dynasty: Fort built by Asa Ahir (Ahir dynasty, early 15th century); captured by Akbar 17 Jan 1601; Maratha-period temple construction associated with Ahilyabai Holkar's patronage (18th century, per some sources)
history.period: Shrine antiquity uncertain - local legend claims Mahabharata-era origin; fort 15th century; current temple structure attributed to 18th century
history.summary: Historic Shiva shrine inside the Asirgarh fort, about 20-27 km north of Burhanpur (the 'Key to the Deccan'), known as the Gupteshwar Mahadev Mandir. Local legend holds that Ashwatthama of the Mahabharata worships here each morning - devotees find fresh flowers and sandal offered at dawn - though some sources push the claim to a 5,000-year Mahabharata-era origin (verify - legendary). One travel source attributes the present temple structure to 18th-century Marathi-style construction under Ahilyabai Holkar, while the fort itself was built by Asa Ahir in the early 15th century, seized by Akbar in 1601 after his famous siege, and taken by the British in 1803; fort timings reported 10 AM-5 PM vs temple 9 AM-5 PM (verify - hours conflict). The fort also contains the ruined Asir Masjid and British-era graves. CSV state-column error: the source CSV lists the town in the 'state' column - the site is in Madhya Pradesh.

name: Asirgarh Shiva Temple
town_description: Burhanpur is a historic city in southwest Madhya Pradesh on the Tapti river, once the Mughal capital of the Deccan - famed for the Jama Masjid, Kundi Bhandara water system, and the hilltop Asirgarh fort about 20-27 km north that guarded the pass through the Satpuras.

travel.airport: Indore Airport is the nearest major airport (~183 km per temple travel source - verify).
travel.railway: Burhanpur Railway Station is the nearest major station; the fort is ~20-27 km north of the city.
travel.road: Burhanpur city centre is ~21 km from Asirgarh Fort (per travel sources); the temple is reached by narrow paths a little below fort level inside the complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for the fort visit and the hill climb.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort timings reported as 10:00 AM-5:00 PM (trawell/adotrip); one blog reports temple timings 9:00 AM-5:00 PM (verify - hours conflict between fort and temple sources). Entry free per trawell (adotrip reports a fee - verify).
